newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair seeks Clinton's backing on N. Ireland.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair seeks Clinton's backing on N. Ireland.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair will seek renewed support from U.S. President Bill Clinton for ways of advancing the Northern Ireland peace process ahead of a key statement to parliament next week, officials said on Friday.
They said Blair would discuss Northern Ireland with Clinton on Saturday on the fringes of the Group of Seven major industrialised nations annual summit in Denver, Colorado.

Britain broke off contacts with Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army (IRA), this week after the outlawed guerrilla group killed two policemen in an ambush in the rural town of Lurgan, southwest of Belfast.

Blair recognises that the murder was a serious setback but is determined to redouble his efforts to put the peace process begun by his predecessor, former prime minister John Major, back on track, a senior official said.
"The prime minister's got ideas...He's determined that a way has to be found of going forward," the official said.

Recognising that U.S. opinion has an important bearing on the peace process, he will urge Clinton to use his influence to impress upon the IRA and Sinn Fein that its strategy of using violence and politics interchangeably is unacceptable.
Clinton has given strong backing in the past to the peace process and officials are confident he will do the same again.
"We are very pleased with the messages that have come through both publicly and privately from President Clinton," one official said.
The date for next week's parliamentary statement by the prime minister has not yet been fixed. Blair will brief the leaders of Britain's other political parties in advance.

Blair is looking for early indications from William Hague, who has replaced Major as leader of the main Conservative opposition party, that he will maintain the bipartisan approach to Northern Ireland that has prevailed in recent years.
